title: ST VL53LB is the smallest FlightSense ToF ranging sensor at just 4.0 × 1.8 × 1.0 mm
summary:
STMicroelectronics has just introduced the VL53LB (VL53LBCA), its smallest Time-of-Flight (ToF) ranging sensor, part of the FlightSense portfolio, with a size of just 4.0 × 1.8 × 1.0 mm. Like the earlier VL53L0X and VL53L1X models, it’s a single-zone ToF sensor featuring a 940 nm invisible vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser (VCSEL), but it offers a longer range of up to 8 meters and supports multi-object detection. It’s 30% smaller than the previous generation (VL53L3) and consumes just 50 µW in ULP mode, which makes it ideal for smartphones and space-constrained robotics and industrial systems. title: TinyWifiDongle Arduino library turns ESP32-S3 and Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W boards into USB WiFi adapters
summary:
TinyWifiDongle open-source Arduino library turns ESP32-S2/S3 and Raspberry Pi Pico W/2 W boards into USB WiFi adapters. The library uses USB CDC-NCM (Network Control Model) to provide network connectivity to Linux, macOS, and Windows 11 computers without installing additional drivers. The library implements a transparent Layer-2 bridge between the MCU’s WiFi and USB interfaces, allowing the connected computer to get an IP address directly from the router via DHCP, without NAT or a separate network. It supports hard-coded WiFi credentials or browser-based configuration and achieves approximately 5 Mbps on the ESP32-S3 and 2 Mbps on the Pico 2 W in the developer’s tests. TinyWifiDongle overview: Supported hardware ESP32-S3 and ESP32-S2 with native USB-OTG support; tested on ESP32-S3 Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W (RP2350) and Pico W (RP2040); tested on Pico 2 W ESP32-P4 (+ESP32-C6) support is experimental, with USB networking not yet tested USB networking – USB CDC-NCM using TinyUSB [...]

InMachines Ingrassia GmbH has launched the Piccola CNC, an open-source hardware desktop CNC milling machine designed for PCB prototyping and machining wood, plastics, and soft metals such as aluminum, brass, and copper. Built in Germany, the machine features a 150 × 150 × 70 mm work area, belt-driven ball screws on all three axes, ER11 collets, and a choice of 100W or 200W spindles. The machine comes in three versions, which include the Basic, Pro, and Ultimate. The Pro variant adds a full enclosure and safety interlocks, while the Ultimate model further adds a brushless spindle and laser distance sensor. Other features include USB-C and Wi-Fi connectivity, built-in CAM software for PCB, 2D, 3D, and rotary milling, and laser-based PCB height mapping on the Ultimate, with the sensor available as an accessory for Basic and Pro.
